title: Basin returning-woodland composition and succession
scope: Qualitative composition and present successional state of the initial basin's returning woodland, including its first floral-kingdom assignments; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: The basin's returning woodland is composed principally of K2 tower flora with K3 free-seeder thickets, over a ground and surface layer of K5 crust-and-cushion flora and K6 thread decomposers.
Its present state is young; seventy years is short against tower replacement rates.
When organised suppression ended, buried K3 vault banks under abandoned clearances woke and erupted, and today's woodland is chiefly that result.
The prevailing structure is dense, tangled vault-seeder thicket giving way patchily to young towers that have risen but not thickened.
Scattered relict old towers survive from before the clearances, recognisable by their bulk and deep-layered casings and often carrying heavy crust-and-cushion cover on older casing faces.
Mature timber-analogue material is scarce; the woodland is rich in thin stems and poor in old ones, making relict towers locally valuable and their felling consequential.
Passage through young thicket is harder than through mature woodland.
Lineage II browsing contests the woodland's advance, so its boundary moves in some places and is held back in others, and succession is not uniform across the basin.
boundaries: Thicket, relict tower, and young tower are author-facing descriptive terms, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
Kingdom assignment is compositional only; it establishes no species, names, taxonomy, member inventory, or proportion beyond the qualitative principal-and-layer description.

Exact extent, boundaries, density, canopy height, patch sizes, and the woodland's relationship to the western rainforest and damp refugia remain open; the rainforest's own composition is not established here.
Relict-tower abundance, distribution, sizes, ages, condition, and recognisability to any observer remain open; no particular tree, stand, or place is established.

Locally valuable describes ecological and material scarcity, not price, ownership, law, custom, protection, or any established practice; no timber, fuel, forage, coppice, clearance, or management practice is established.
Harder passage is qualitative; no speed, travel time, route, or impassability is established, and the lake road's accepted planning anchors are unaffected.

Woken vault banks explain the thicket's origin as the prevailing pattern, not an exclusive one; dispersal-founded growth and surviving stands remain possible, and no particular clearance is established as having carried a bank.

Contested advance establishes qualitative browsing pressure only; it fixes no boundary position, browsing intensity, opening size, or rate, and identifies no particular field, road segment, or lake approach as a crown-herd overlap.
Raised surface-fire exposure follows from dense young growth and permitted dry spells; no fire frequency, season, severity, extent, or event is established.
Deadfall accumulation and whether the woodland's thread-decomposer population is sufficient to process it remain open.
The woodland's age structure is a physical consequence of the collapse; no in-world knowledge, dating practice, or ability to read it is established.
No animal is established as inhabiting, feeding, breeding, or sheltering in the thicket, and no lineage is assigned to any woodland animal.
Earth life may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
No System mechanic, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, specialised Mana ability, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Soil, water, light, nutrients, growth time, disturbance, browsing, disease, and decay remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Scenes can show tangled young thicket, slow blind travel off the road, and crust-covered relict towers standing out of the regrowth.
The settlement lives with abundant small stems and fuel but scarce structural material.
Browsed openings give the woodland edge a contested, shifting character.
Dry spells carry raised fire risk in dense young growth.
Every place, practice, encounter, and event requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The composition describes ordinary succession and disturbance ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: Which tower and free-seeder members compose the woodland, and in what proportions?
How abundant are relict towers, and where do they concentrate?
What woodland uses does the settlement actually practise given the stem-size asymmetry?
How frequent and severe is surface fire in the thicket, and how does it interact with vault banks?
Is the young woodland's decomposer population sufficient for its deadfall?
Which animals inhabit the thicket, and from which lineages?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C succession-state cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Thicket-and-relict' on 2026-08-17.
